items.claim: The row's stated internal-cohesion ground -- one first-person divine speaker running from Isa.29.2 through Isa.29.8 -- is contradicted by the bytes, and an accent-stripped-tier divine-title formula straddles the row's own front seam undisclosed.
items.evidence: The row's cohesion ground for holding Isa.29.5-Isa.29.8 with the siege announcement is stated as one first-person divine speaker carried through Isa.29.8; the bytes do not carry that. First-person forms are confined to Isa.29.2-Isa.29.4 -- וַהֲצִיק֖וֹתִי (oshb:Isa.29.2, byte tier), וְחָנִ֥יתִי and וְצַרְתִּ֤י (oshb:Isa.29.3, byte tier) -- while Isa.29.5-Isa.29.8 carries none of them and Isa.29.6 names the deity in the third person, מֵעִ֨ם יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ תִּפָּקֵ֔ד (oshb:Isa.29.6, byte tier), matched by both witnesses (“She will be visited by Yahweh of Armies” web:Isa.29.6). The person change at Isa.29.5 is a seam signal the row denies rather than weighs; the complex may still hold together, but not on the ground given. Second, a byte-true device straddles the row's own front seam undisclosed: the of-hosts formula מֵעִ֛ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת stands at oshb:Isa.28.29, the verse immediately before the seam, and recurs inside the row at oshb:Isa.29.6 at accent-stripped tier (sweep: 3 verses book-wide at that tier -- oshb:Isa.8.18, oshb:Isa.28.29, oshb:Isa.29.6); it argues continuity across the seam and owes disclosure even though the woe onset outweighs it. Verified sound: ה֚וֹי is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.29.1 (byte tier) and belongs to the chapters-28-33 woe series (sweep: 22 hoy verses book-wide, 20 of them verse-initial); the doubled address is byte-true; and the setumah disclosures at Isa.28.29 and Isa.29.8 agree with the single-witness inventory and exhaust what bears on this span (sweep: 209 marked verses book-wide; 10 in chapters 29-30 -- a petuchah at Isa.30.14 and setumah at Isa.29.8, Isa.29.12, Isa.29.14, Isa.29.21, Isa.30.5, Isa.30.11, Isa.30.18, Isa.30.26, Isa.30.33).

items.claim: The row's opener is labelled a vocative onset where the bytes carry imperative forms without a vocative element, and its non-dividing argument at Isa.29.13 rests on a constant addressee the bytes contradict.
items.evidence: Two byte-level grounds fail. (1) The opener is declared a vocative onset, but הִתְמַהְמְה֣וּ וּתְמָ֔הוּ הִשְׁתַּֽעַשְׁע֖וּ וָשֹׁ֑עוּ (oshb:Isa.29.9, byte tier) carries four second-person plural imperative forms, without a vocative particle or an addressee noun; both witnesses render commands (“Pause and wonder! Blind yourselves and be blind!” web:Isa.29.9), so the signal in the bytes is an imperative onset rather than a vocative. (2) The frame at Isa.29.13 is held to be non-dividing on the ground that the addressee stays constant; the bytes give a different addressee before and after that frame. Second-person plural forms run through the preceding verses -- עֲלֵיכֶ֤ם and עֵֽינֵיכֶ֑ם (oshb:Isa.29.10, byte tier), לָכֶ֜ם (oshb:Isa.29.11, byte tier) -- and drop out at Isa.29.13-Isa.29.14, where first-person divine speech names its object in the third person: הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה with כִּבְּד֔וּנִי and מִמֶּ֑נִּי (oshb:Isa.29.13, byte tier). The voice turns as well: Isa.29.10 speaks of the deity in the third person, Isa.29.13 speaks as the deity. The frame form itself is a bare-adonai form, וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲדֹנָ֗י (oshb:Isa.29.13, byte tier), and the row leaves its speaker class unnamed, which this book's bare-adonai census (sweep: 51 verses book-wide) requires because the same token carries a courtly role elsewhere. Third, the rear seam is crossed undisclosed by the scroll catchword: הַסֵּ֣פֶר (oshb:Isa.29.11, byte tier) and סֵֽפֶר (oshb:Isa.29.12, byte tier) recur at דִּבְרֵי סֵ֑פֶר (oshb:Isa.29.18, byte tier), outside this span (sweep: 4 verses at consonantal-skeleton tier in chapters 28-31 -- Isa.29.11, Isa.29.12, Isa.29.18, Isa.30.8). Verified sound: the ketiv/qere handling is exact -- the doubled token pair sits later in oshb:Isa.29.11 than the quoted English run ends -- and the setumah disclosures at Isa.29.8, Isa.29.12 and Isa.29.14 agree with the single-witness inventory and exhaust what bears on this span (sweep: 209 marked verses book-wide; 10 in chapters 29-30 -- a petuchah at Isa.30.14 and setumah at Isa.29.8, Isa.29.12, Isa.29.14, Isa.29.21, Isa.30.5, Isa.30.11, Isa.30.18, Isa.30.26, Isa.30.33).

items.claim: The row's divine-title cohesion evidence rests on one in-span occurrence argued from the English rendering, and the scroll catchword crossing its front seam is undisclosed; its potter-and-clay catchword claim, by contrast, is byte-true and correctly tiered.
items.evidence: The divine-title evidence is overstated and rests on the translation. The title-construct occurs in this span at one site, בִּקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.29.19, byte tier); the recurrence chain lies outside the span (sweep: 25 title verses book-wide; in chapters 28-31 at Isa.29.19, Isa.30.11, Isa.30.12, Isa.30.15, Isa.31.1), so one occurrence cannot show that one voice runs through the row, and the claim is evidenced from the English rendering without quoting a Hebrew form or naming a tier -- insufficient engagement for a signal the row declares among its drivers. The front seam is also crossed undisclosed by the scroll catchword: הַסֵּ֣פֶר at oshb:Isa.29.11 and סֵֽפֶר at oshb:Isa.29.12 recur inside this span at דִּבְרֵי סֵ֑פֶר (oshb:Isa.29.18, byte tier) (sweep: 4 verses at consonantal-skeleton tier in chapters 28-31), which argues that the blindness complex continues across Isa.29.14|Isa.29.15. Verified sound and credited: ה֛וֹי is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.29.15 (byte tier) and is a member of the chapters-28-33 woe series (sweep: 20 verse-initial hoy verses book-wide); the shared verb claim is exactly right and honestly tiered -- יֵֽחָשֵׁ֑ב (oshb:Isa.29.16, byte tier) against יֵחָשֵֽׁב (oshb:Isa.29.17, byte tier) differ in accent and meteg placement, so they meet only at consonantal-skeleton tier (sweep: 5 verses book-wide at that tier -- Isa.10.7, Isa.13.17, Isa.29.16, Isa.29.17, Isa.32.15, the sole adjacent pair among them); the setumah disclosures at Isa.29.14 and Isa.29.21 agree with the single-witness inventory and exhaust what bears on this span (sweep: 209 marked verses book-wide; 10 in chapters 29-30 -- a petuchah at Isa.30.14 and setumah at Isa.29.8, Isa.29.12, Isa.29.14, Isa.29.21, Isa.30.5, Isa.30.11, Isa.30.18, Isa.30.26, Isa.30.33).

items.claim: The boundary at Isa.29.21|Isa.29.22 is carried by a divine messenger formula whose form, owner and named addressee sit in the cited verse's bytes, and whose disclosures check out.
items.evidence: The cut stands on its own bytes. לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל בֵּ֣ית יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב (oshb:Isa.29.22, byte tier) places the messenger formula in the cited verse with the claimed role, names its owner as the tetragrammaton rather than leaving the formula unattributed, and carries an explicit addressee -- and that addressee is the byte feature separating this site from the otherwise identical construction at oshb:Isa.30.12, where the formula stands without one (sweep: 6 verses book-wide carry the connector-plus-formula string at consonantal-skeleton tier; in chapters 28-33 at Isa.28.16, Isa.29.22, Isa.30.12). The rear seam is a verse-initial woe onset, ה֣וֹי (oshb:Isa.30.1, byte tier). The mark layer is handled correctly: the setumah at Isa.29.21 agrees with the single-witness inventory, the span itself carries none (sweep: 209 marked verses book-wide; 10 in chapters 29-30 -- a petuchah at Isa.30.14 and setumah at Isa.29.8, Isa.29.12, Isa.29.14, Isa.29.21, Isa.30.5, Isa.30.11, Isa.30.18, Isa.30.26, Isa.30.33), and the row records that as disclosure rather than as evidence. Two observations that do not disturb the cut: the frame's own head לָכֵ֗ן is this book's consequence connector, standing within these two chapters at Isa.29.14, Isa.29.22, Isa.30.7, Isa.30.12, Isa.30.13 and Isa.30.18 (sweep: 25 verses book-wide at consonantal-skeleton tier), so the frame binds backwards as well as opening; and the span's own divine-title pileup קְד֣וֹשׁ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב with אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.29.23, byte tier) is a distinct object from the title four verses earlier and goes unengaged.

items.claim: A clause repeated at consonantal-skeleton tier across the row's own rear seam is left undisclosed while the row records high confidence, and the rival reading is stated without its byte grounds.
items.evidence: The row's rear seam is crossed by a repeated clause that the row leaves undisclosed, while it records high confidence. עַל עַ֖ם לֹא יוֹעִ֣ילוּ לָ֑מוֹ stands at oshb:Isa.30.5 (byte tier) and oshb:Isa.30.6 ends on עַל עַ֖ם לֹ֥א יוֹעִֽילוּ (byte tier); the two meet at consonantal-skeleton tier and at no higher tier (the accent-stripped tier separates them), and the clause occurs in exactly two verses book-wide at that tier (sweep: 2 verses -- Isa.30.5, Isa.30.6). The Egypt naming crosses the same seam: מִצְרַ֔יִם and מִצְרָֽיִם (oshb:Isa.30.2, byte tier), מִצְרַ֖יִם (oshb:Isa.30.3, byte tier), then וּמִצְרַ֕יִם (oshb:Isa.30.7, byte tier) (sweep: 40 verses book-wide; in chapters 28-31 at Isa.30.2, Isa.30.3, Isa.30.7, Isa.31.1, Isa.31.3). A byte-true device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity across it unless disclosed; the row offers a bare rival sentence without byte grounds, which is what leaves the high confidence unearned rather than the cut itself wrong. Verified sound: the stacked onset ה֣וֹי בָּנִ֤ים סֽוֹרְרִים֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.30.1, byte tier) is a verse-initial woe with the postpositive signature attached (sweep: 19 verses book-wide carry that signature-plus-name string at consonantal-skeleton tier); the ketiv/qere statement is accurate, since the doubled token pair stands at the head of oshb:Isa.30.5 and the quoted English run is that verse's closing clause; the setumah disclosure at Isa.30.5 agrees with the single-witness inventory (sweep: 209 marked verses book-wide; 10 in chapters 29-30 -- a petuchah at Isa.30.14 and setumah at Isa.29.8, Isa.29.12, Isa.29.14, Isa.29.21, Isa.30.5, Isa.30.11, Isa.30.18, Isa.30.26, Isa.30.33).

items.claim: The row cuts correctly on a verse-initial burden header but describes the rival as thematic when the bytes repeat a clause across that seam, understating the counter-weight on a low-band hold.
items.evidence: The row's rival disclosure misstates the counter-evidence. It rests the rival on theme -- both sides concerning reliance on Egypt, with no addressee shift between them -- but the bytes repeat a clause across the very seam the row cuts: עַל עַ֖ם לֹא יוֹעִ֣ילוּ לָ֑מוֹ at oshb:Isa.30.5 (byte tier) against the closing עַל עַ֖ם לֹ֥א יוֹעִֽילוּ at oshb:Isa.30.6 (byte tier), meeting at consonantal-skeleton tier in exactly two verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses -- Isa.30.5, Isa.30.6). The header verse therefore ends on the same clause the preceding verse turns on, which is textual continuity rather than thematic continuity, and the Egypt naming runs across the seam as well (מִצְרַ֔יִם at oshb:Isa.30.2, byte tier; וּמִצְרַ֕יִם at oshb:Isa.30.7, byte tier). Because this row is held at a low band, understating the counter-weight is the defect that matters -- the hold is honest, its grounds are not complete. Verified sound: מַשָּׂ֖א בַּהֲמ֣וֹת נֶ֑גֶב (oshb:Isa.30.6, byte tier) is verse-initial and is the construct-header form, properly kept apart from the burden common noun מַשָּׂאָ֑ה at oshb:Isa.30.27 (byte tier), which a contiguous consonantal search would otherwise blend (sweep: 15 verses carry that skeleton book-wide, of which 10 are verse-initial headers); the rear-seam opener עַתָּ֗ה בּ֣וֹא (oshb:Isa.30.8, byte tier) is unique in the book (sweep: 1 verse at consonantal-skeleton tier); the English header quote agrees with the staged folded text at this fold site; the setumah disclosure at Isa.30.5 agrees with the single-witness inventory (sweep: 209 marked verses book-wide; 10 in chapters 29-30 -- a petuchah at Isa.30.14 and setumah at Isa.29.8, Isa.29.12, Isa.29.14, Isa.29.21, Isa.30.5, Isa.30.11, Isa.30.18, Isa.30.26, Isa.30.33).

items.claim: The row's messenger-frame and divine-title signals are asserted from the English rendering, without a pointed form, a tier or a named frame owner -- at the one site in the span where the frame is owned by a non-adjacent title.
items.evidence: The row's two Hebrew-dependent signals are argued from the English rendering. The messenger frames it declares at Isa.30.12 and Isa.30.15 are לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Isa.30.12, byte tier) and כִּ֣י כֹֽה אָמַר֩ אֲדֹנָ֨י יְהוִ֜ה קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל (oshb:Isa.30.15, byte tier) -- both divine frames -- yet neither Hebrew form is quoted and the frame owner is left unnamed, which matters most at oshb:Isa.30.12 because there the frame is owned by the title rather than by an adjacent divine name, so an unnamed owner cannot be checked (sweep: 48 messenger-formula verses book-wide, role-split before any digit). The title claim rests on the translation as well: the sites are אֶת קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Isa.30.11, byte tier), קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Isa.30.12, byte tier) and קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל (oshb:Isa.30.15, byte tier), so the three-fold count is correct (sweep: 25 title verses book-wide), but a title used to argue internal coherence needs its pointed form and its tier, not three translation quotations. Separately, the commission is assigned to the prophet; the bytes give second-person masculine singular imperatives בּ֣וֹא כָתְבָ֥הּ (oshb:Isa.30.8, byte tier) and name no addressee, so the singular-against-plural contrast is byte-supported while the referent is not carried by the verse. Verified sound: the opener is unique in the book -- עַתָּ֗ה בּ֣וֹא (oshb:Isa.30.8, byte tier), sweep: 1 verse at consonantal-skeleton tier; both marked divisions inside the span are disclosed under the correct, unconflated types -- a setumah at Isa.30.11 and a petuchah at Isa.30.14 -- and agree with the single-witness inventory (sweep: 209 marked verses book-wide; 10 in chapters 29-30 -- a petuchah at Isa.30.14 and setumah at Isa.29.8, Isa.29.12, Isa.29.14, Isa.29.21, Isa.30.5, Isa.30.11, Isa.30.18, Isa.30.26, Isa.30.33).

items.claim: The row's opener is a consequence connector rather than a temporal turn, and the speaking voice changes at the front seam instead of continuing -- so both stated grounds fail even though the boundary itself is sound.
items.evidence: Both front-seam grounds are byte-false. The row calls its opener a fresh temporal turn under the same speaking voice; its own quoted form וְלָכֵ֞ן יְחַכֶּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Isa.30.18, byte tier) names the deity in the third person, while the verses it turns from are divine speech under כִּ֣י כֹֽה אָמַר֩ אֲדֹנָ֨י יְהוִ֜ה קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל (oshb:Isa.30.15, byte tier) addressing second-person plural -- גְּבֽוּרַתְכֶ֑ם and אֲבִיתֶֽם at oshb:Isa.30.15 (byte tier), תָּנֻ֑סוּ and נוֹתַרְתֶּ֗ם at oshb:Isa.30.17 (byte tier). Both witnesses show the same turn (“For thus said the Lord Yahweh” web:Isa.30.15 against “Therefore Yahweh will wait” web:Isa.30.18), so the voice changes at the row's front boundary rather than staying the same. And וְלָכֵ֞ן is this book's consequence connector rather than a temporal marker: oshb:Isa.30.18 carries no temporal element, and the same particle stands at Isa.29.14, Isa.29.22, Isa.30.7, Isa.30.12 and Isa.30.13 (sweep: 25 verses book-wide at consonantal-skeleton tier). The net effect is that the boundary is better supported than the row argues while the reasons given for it fail. One disclosure gap: the span carries a paseq seg at Isa.30.25 (count-only, single-witness, position unsourceable; sweep: 95 segs over 87 verses book-wide, 1 of them in chapters 29-30) which the row omits while engaging the marked-division layer at Isa.30.18 and Isa.30.26 -- those two setumah citations do agree with the single-witness inventory (sweep: 209 marked verses book-wide; 10 in chapters 29-30 -- a petuchah at Isa.30.14 and setumah at Isa.29.8, Isa.29.12, Isa.29.14, Isa.29.21, Isa.30.5, Isa.30.11, Isa.30.18, Isa.30.26, Isa.30.33).
